wolt.json.unit: period (not calendar week) - Wolt's own Hexa invoicing cycle, usually ~5 days
wolt.json.schema: periodEnd, period, invoiceNo, invoiceDate, wolt_fee_net/vat/gross, orderFees_net/gross, deliveryServiceFees_net/gross, lateFees_gross (optional), adSpend_net/gross (optional), invoiceTotal_gross, revenue_goods_net/gross, revenue_delivery_service_net/gross, payoutCorrections, payoutAmount, driveFileIds{merchantInvoice,payoutReport,salesReport}
wolt.json.source_docs_per_period: 3 files: merchant invoice (fees), payout report (revenue+payout), sales report (order detail) - all 3 needed for full picture, but merchant invoice alone gives fee data if others missing

uber_eats.json.unit: calendar week (Mon-Sun), sourced from weekly 'Aktivitätsübersicht' (activity overview) PDF
uber_eats.json.schema: periodStart, periodEnd, reportDate, orders, grossOrderValue, discounts, netAfterDiscounts, commissions{uberDelivery33pct_orders/amt, uberDelivery30pct_orders/amt, ownDelivery13pct_orders/amt, pickup13pct_orders/amt}, uberEatsFee_net/vat, marketing{adsGross,offerFeeGross}, misc{deliveryFeesCollected,tips,refunds,vatRounding,other,cashCollected}, payoutTotal, driveFileId, officialInvoiceFileId+officialInvoiceNo (optional, when the formal tax invoice for that week's fee is also found)
uber_eats.json.authoritative_monthly_source: Uber also provides a 'sales-over-time' CSV export (month-by-month gross sales + order count) which is MORE reliable than summing weekly Aktivitätsübersicht PDFs - use this for revenue_monthly.json's monthly 'uber' figure whenever the user uploads or you can locate one. Confirmed exact match Jan-Jul 2026 against previously-built weekly-derived figures.

lieferando.json.unit: Lieferando's own weekly billing period (Mon-Sun), sourced from weekly invoice
lieferando.json.schema: periodStart, periodEnd, invoiceDate, invoiceNo, orders, revenue_gross, serviceFee30pct, topRankFee, onlinePaymentAdminFee, pickupFee14pct, subtotal_net, vat19, invoiceTotal_gross, tips (optional), chargebacks (optional), payoutAmount, driveFileId
lieferando.json.authoritative_calendar_month_source: Lieferando also provides 'online_payments_report' CSVs (one per calendar month, per-order Date/description/Amount rows, format Date;Description;"XX,XX €"). These give CALENDAR-MONTH-aligned totals, which differ slightly (~1%) from the weekly-invoice-period sums used to build revenue_monthly.json's monthly 'lieferando' figures, because Lieferando's billing weeks cross month boundaries. When available, prefer the online_payments_report CSV total for revenue_monthly.json's monthly figure - it's what actually reconciles to calendar-month bookkeeping. As of 2026-08-15 all 8 months (Jan-Aug 2026) were replaced with this source.

cutoff_date_tracking.method: Before any rescan, first fetch manifest.json (suppliers) or the relevant platform JSON's periods/weeks array (delivery platforms) to find the current latestInvoiceDate / periodEnd per source. Then search Drive with modifiedTime > that cutoff, NOT a round-numbered date - tighter cutoffs mean fewer stale/duplicate re-fetches per rescan.
cutoff_date_tracking.duplicate_files_are_common: Google Drive frequently has near-duplicate files for the same invoice (different filename, same content, re-uploaded/re-synced) - always dedupe by invoiceNo/date against what's already in the JSON before adding, not just by filename.

known_technical_quirks.google_drive_search_files_broken_for_non: google_drive_search tool (legacy) is broken for non-Google-Doc files - use Google Drive:search_files with query = "parentId = '[folder_id]'" instead, optionally with "and modifiedTime > 'ISO_DATE'"
known_technical_quirks.download_file_content_vs_read_file_conte: download_file_content returns raw base64 (accurate but must decode yourself, large files get saved to a tool_results JSON file with a 'text' field containing the wrapper JSON with a base64 'content' field - extract via python, don't hand-copy). read_file_content returns human-readable text but applies MARKDOWN ESCAPING (backslash before _#[]) which must be stripped via regex before json.loads. For large files (>50KB) prefer download_file_content and process via bash/python entirely programmatically - do NOT hand-transcribe base64 or escaped text into a python heredoc, this is extremely error-prone (caused real corruption/brace-mismatch bugs in earlier sessions) and burns huge amounts of context.
known_technical_quirks.github_api_not_raw_for_writes: Always GET the current sha via api.github.com before PUT (write) - raw.githubusercontent.com can serve stale cached content and using its content as a base for edits risks clobbering newer commits.
known_technical_quirks.bash_argument_list_too_long: Very large base64 strings (>~150KB) can blow the shell's argument list limit when passed via python -c "...". Write large payloads to a JSON file first (python script that writes directly to a .json file) then reference that file with curl -d @file.json, rather than inlining huge strings in a shell command.
